title: Affine gluing of independent semilocal subrings of a field
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $r\geq1$, and let $A_1,\ldots,A_r\subseteq K$ be unital subrings with fraction field $K$. Suppose each $A_i$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], semilocal (has finitely many maximal ideals), and of Krull dimension exactly one [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Suppose that for all $i\ne j$ the map $A_i\otimes_{\mathbb Z}A_j\to K$, $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$, is surjective [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. There is a Noetherian semilocal domain $A\subseteq\bigcap_i A_i$, of dimension one and with fraction field $K$, such that the inclusions $A\to A_i$ induce open immersions $j_i:\operatorname{Spec}(A_i)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion], their images cover $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, and each closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ lies in exactly one image. If all $A_i$ are local, their closed points map to pairwise distinct points $m_i$ which are exactly the closed points of $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, and the inclusions identify $A_{m_i}$ with $A_i$; for $i\ne j$, the intersection of the two open subschemes is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}(K)$, with its maps to both charts induced by the given inclusions in $K$.

source.place: Tag 09N4 (varieties-lemma-glue-a-bunch-of-local-rings), statement and proof; local-ring consequences used explicitly in Tag 09NJ (varieties-lemma-finite-set-codim-1-points-in-affine), proof, displayed open covering and sentence preceding it.

proof.text: Prove by induction on $s\geq1$ the stronger construction $R_s=\bigcap_{i=1}^s A_i$: it is a Noetherian semilocal domain of dimension one with fraction field $K$, and its given inclusions induce an open cover by the first $s$ spectra. For $s=1$ take $R_1=A_1$ and the identity open immersion. The identity has the required properties by the hypotheses and [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Tag 09N4 (varieties-lemma-glue-a-bunch-of-local-rings), proof; expanded induction and its local-ring consequences in Tag 09NJ (varieties-lemma-finite-set-codim-1-points-in-affine).

proof.text: For the induction step write $B=\bigcap_{i=2}^s A_i$ and apply the induction hypothesis to this smaller family. We first prove $A_1\otimes_{\mathbb Z}B\to K$ surjective. Otherwise [lem-trf-one-dimensional-subrings-common-dvr-criterion] gives a proper DVR $V\subset K$ containing $A_1$ and $B$. Let $\mathfrak n=B\cap\mathfrak m_V$. It is nonzero: if it were zero, every nonzero element of $B$ would be a unit in $V$, so $K=\operatorname{Frac}B\subseteq V$, a contradiction. Thus $\mathfrak n$ is maximal since $\dim B=1$. Choose a chart $\operatorname{Spec}A_j$ of the induction cover containing $\mathfrak n$, with prime $\mathfrak q$ above it. Open immersion and affine-stalk identification give $B_{\mathfrak n}\cong(A_j)_{\mathfrak q}$ compatibly inside $K$ ([def-weil-open-immersion], [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field]). Since $B\subset V$ and every element of $B\setminus\mathfrak n$ is a unit in $V$, the fraction description of localization gives $B_{\mathfrak n}\subset V$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Hence $A_j\subseteq V$. This contradicts the common-DVR criterion applied to $A_1,A_j$, whose tensor map is surjective by hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 09N4 (varieties-lemma-glue-a-bunch-of-local-rings), proof; expanded induction and its local-ring consequences in Tag 09NJ (varieties-lemma-finite-set-codim-1-points-in-affine).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-two-semilocal-rings-intersection-cover] to $A_1,B$, now that their multiplication tensor map is surjective. Its other hypotheses hold for $A_1$ by assumption and for $B$ by induction. It gives the two open charts covering $\operatorname{Spec}R_s$ for $R_s=A_1\cap B$. Composing the induction charts inside $\operatorname{Spec}B$ yields the desired cover by all $A_i$: composites are open immersions because the homeomorphisms onto open subsets and the structure-sheaf isomorphisms in [def-weil-open-immersion] compose. By functoriality of spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum] these are precisely the morphisms of the given inclusions.

source.place: Tag 09N4 (varieties-lemma-glue-a-bunch-of-local-rings), proof; expanded induction and its local-ring consequences in Tag 09NJ (varieties-lemma-finite-set-codim-1-points-in-affine).

proof.text: The intersection $R_s\subset K$ is a domain. Each chart sends its zero prime to the zero prime of $R_s$, by contraction along an inclusion. The affine-stalk formula [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field] and the open-immersion sheaf isomorphism identify $(R_s)_{(0)}$ with $(A_1)_{(0)}=K$ inside $K$; thus $K$ is its fraction field. For any chain of primes of $R_s$, choose a chart containing its largest prime. All the smaller primes are also in that open: Zariski opens are stable under generalization, since a basic neighborhood $D(f)$ of a prime contains every smaller prime. The chart is a homeomorphism onto its image, so prime-chain lengths are at most one. Conversely a chain $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak q$ in $A_1$ stays strict under the injective chart map. Hence $\dim R_s=1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Every maximal prime of $R_s$ is nonzero, and in any chart over it the prime is nonzero, hence maximal in that one-dimensional domain. Consequently the maximal primes of $R_s$ lie in the finite union of the images of the maximal primes of all the semilocal $A_i$. This proves semilocality.

source.place: Tag 09N4 (varieties-lemma-glue-a-bunch-of-local-rings), proof; expanded induction and its local-ring consequences in Tag 09NJ (varieties-lemma-finite-set-codim-1-points-in-affine).

proof.text: The affine open cover by spectra of the Noetherian $A_i$ makes $\operatorname{Spec}R_s$ locally Noetherian by the affine-cover definition [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Apply [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth] to its whole affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R_s$ to conclude that $R_s$ is Noetherian. This completes the inductive claim; take $A=R_r$.

source.place: Tag 01OW (properties-lemma-locally-Noetherian), equivalence of (2) and (3); used implicitly for Noetherianity in varieties Tag 09N4.

proof.text: Let a closed point $\mathfrak m$ of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ belong to both charts $i\ne j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field] and [def-weil-open-immersion] both $A_i$ and $A_j$ embed in $A_{\mathfrak m}\subset K$, and the maps agree with their inclusions into $K$. Therefore every finite sum of products $a_i a_j$ lies in $A_{\mathfrak m}$. Tensor-map surjectivity implies $K\subseteq A_{\mathfrak m}$, so $A_{\mathfrak m}=K$. But $A$ is a dimension-one domain and $\mathfrak m$ is maximal, so $\mathfrak m\ne0$; a nonzero element of $\mathfrak m$ remains nonzero and noninvertible in $A_{\mathfrak m}$ by the fraction description [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. This contradicts its being a field. Thus every closed point lies in exactly one chart, existence following from the cover.

source.place: Tag 09N4 (varieties-lemma-glue-a-bunch-of-local-rings), proof; expanded induction and its local-ring consequences in Tag 09NJ (varieties-lemma-finite-set-codim-1-points-in-affine).

proof.text: If each $A_i$ is local, its unique maximal ideal is nonzero. Its image $m_i$ is nonzero because each chart is injective on points and takes $(0)$ to $(0)$, and therefore $m_i$ is maximal in the dimension-one domain $A$. Every maximal ideal of $A$ comes from a maximal ideal of a chart by Step 4, so the $m_i$ exhaust the closed points; Step 6 makes them pairwise distinct. The stalk isomorphism gives $A_{m_i}\cong(A_i)_{\mathfrak m_{A_i}}=A_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field] and [def-weil-open-immersion]; the last equality holds since all denominators outside the maximal ideal of a local ring are already units. For $i\ne j$ the intersection of the chart images contains their common generic point and contains no nonzero prime, since all nonzero primes of $A$ are closed. It is thus the open singleton $(0)$, whose structure sheaf has ring $A_{(0)}=K$. The affine-spectrum and stalk identifications identify this open subscheme with $\operatorname{Spec}K$. All identifications use the inclusions into $K$, so its two maps are precisely the maps induced by $A_i,A_j\subset K$.
